content.text: caution with other QTc-prolonging drugs (eg, Class 1A and Class 3 antiarrhythmics, citalopram, erythromycin, levofloxacin, methadone, ziprasidone) and with drugs causing electrolyte imbalance (eg, diuretics, corticosteroids). Potent CYP3A4 inducers (eg, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampin, St John's wort) may lower haloperidol levels enough to reduce efficacy. With lithium, an encephalopathic syndrome followed by irreversible brain damage has occurred in a few patients.

mainly severe EPS, hypotension or sedation; consider the risk of ECG changes associated with torsades. No specific antidote, so treatment is supportive; dialysis isn't recommended. For hypotension use IV fluids, plasma or albumin and vasopressors (eg, phenylephrine, norepinephrine); epinephrine must not be used. Give antiparkinson medication for severe EPS, and monitor the ECG until it is normal.
